before: Heat and pressure without complete melting can form metamorphic rock.
after: Heat and pressure can change solid rock into metamorphic rock without melting the material being metamorphosed.
reason: Independent review: complete source-rock melting is not required for igneous formation.

before: Complete melting followed by cooling and crystallisation produces igneous rock.
after: A melt that cools and crystallises produces igneous rock; the melt can come from partial melting of a source rock.
reason: Independent review: complete source-rock melting is not required for igneous formation.
before_html: Complete melting followed by cooling and crystallisation produces igneous rock.

before: Complete melting; metamorphism changes rock in solid form, whereas melted material that cools forms igneous rock.
after: Metamorphism changes rock in solid form; igneous rock forms when a melt cools and crystallises, even when only part of the source rock melted.
reason: Independent review: complete source-rock melting is not required for igneous formation.
